title: Help Him, He helps you
hook: if you support Allah's cause, He will support you and make your feet firm (47:7)

segments.voice: Yesterday: jinn, the hidden ones, who hushed each other to listen. Your line was even the jinn listened.

Here's a riddle from inside the Qur'an. More than once it calls Allah al-Ghani, the one who needs nothing: not food, not praise, not help. And yet in the forty-seventh surah, a verse speaks to believers as if they could help Him. If ye help Allah, it says. How do you help someone who needs nothing? The surah is named after the Prophet ﷺ himself: Surah Muhammad. And this riddle sits near its opening.

Verse seven, in Pickthall's translation: "O ye who believe! If ye help Allah, He will help you and will make your foothold firm." Ibn Kathir and other commentators answer the riddle this way: helping Allah means helping His cause: His religion, His messenger, His command to do justice and care for the weak. Allah doesn't need the help. The people do, and so, in a sense, do the helpers. The verse is an invitation to stand on the side of good, with a promise attached. The Arabic word for help here is nasr, the word behind Surah An-Nasr, the help, and the name Nasir, helper. And the promise is physical: your feet made firm. Picture standing on a slope in loose sand, then picture planted feet. That's the image. Not wealth, not an easy road. Footing. The surah is counted among those revealed in Medina, in years of conflict, and its first audience heard steadiness in battle. Later readers also heard ordinary courage: the steadiness to keep doing right when it costs something. One more thing about this surah's name. The name Muhammad appears in the Qur'an only four times, and this surah's second verse is one of them. Ahmad, another form of his name, appears once more, in Surah As-Saff. For a book so centered on him, it names him rarely. Mostly it calls him the Messenger, the Prophet, or simply addresses him: you.
screen: `HELP HIS CAUSE, NOT HIM.` · `NASR: HELP, AS IN SURAH AN-NASR.` · `THE PROMISE: FEET MADE FIRM.` · `MUHAMMAD NAMED ONLY FOUR TIMES.`

segments.voice: Stand up for this one, if you can, and feel your feet on the floor; shift your weight until it's even, heels and toes. That's the firmness the verse promises. Standing there, think of one good cause near you, a food bank, a mosque or shelter, a friend's project that does real good, and if you pray, ask for steady feet.
Help Him. In 47:7, to help Allah is to help His cause, and the promise in return is help and feet made firm. Today's word.
Your line: feet made firm. Footing, not an easy road. Day five hundred seventy-eight, done.

howItsDone: Muslims understand helping Allah as supporting good causes, charity, justice and the faith's institutions; many give time and money to mosques, relief funds and community work with this verse in mind.
